The question of whether telepathy is a natural human ability is genuinely contested, with sharply opposing viewpoints across the retrieved evidence. On the scientific side, [d5] (Wikipedia) states that "the scientific consensus is that there is no proof of the existence of such powers, and describes the practice as pseudoscience," and notes that the U.S. National Academy of Sciences concluded there is "no scientific justification from research conducted over a period of 130 years for the existence of parapsychological phenomena." Similarly, [d6] (Aeon) argues that humans do have a natural "sixth sense," but clarifies it "is psychological rather than psychic, made up of an entirely natural and completely human blend of emotional intuition and clever reasoning" — not telepathy in the paranormal sense. [d1] (Smithsonian) further notes that "for nearly all of human history, only the five natural senses were known to serve as a way into the brain," with brain-to-brain communication only recently achieved through technology. On the opposing side, several sources assert telepathy is innate: [d2] claims "Telepathy is a gift that we all possess–and telepathic abilities are much more natural than one might think," [d8] states it is "a natural human ability that we all possess," and [d3] argues telepathy is a natural ability that humans have simply abandoned through long disuse, comparing it to walking after time in a wheelchair. [d7] and [d11] similarly suggest humans once possessed telepathic abilities that have been suppressed by societal influences or disuse. In summary, credible scientific sources [d5] and [d6] find no evidence for telepathy as a natural human ability, while a range of belief-based and anecdotal sources [d2], [d3], [d7], [d8] assert the opposite.
